title: What to Ask for at the Barber: Words That Get You the Cut
hero_alt: A barber checking a client's hair with his hand while the client looks on
card_text: Sides, fade height, top length, neckline and a photo. The words that turn the cut in your head into the one you leave with.
lede: To get the haircut you want, tell your barber five things: how short the sides go, how high the fade or taper starts, how long the top stays, how the neckline is finished, and what happens to the beard. Then show a photo. Those answers and a picture cover almost every cut, and they keep both of us from guessing.
Below is what each term means, a quick guide to clipper guard numbers, and the style names on this site so you can point at the one you want.

subsections.heading: The sides
paragraphs: Fade or taper? A fade takes the sides down short and blends up. A taper only shortens the edges around the ears and at the nape. Then say how short the bottom goes: bare skin, or a little shadow.

subsections.heading: How high
paragraphs: A low fade starts just above the ear, a mid fade around the temple, a high fade near the top of the head. The higher it starts, the more skin shows.

subsections.heading: The top
paragraphs: Say how much to leave, in inches or by holding your fingers apart, and how you wear it: forward, to the side, slicked back or up. Mention texture if you want it choppy instead of one length.

subsections.heading: The neckline
paragraphs: Tapered fades the hair out naturally at the back of the neck. Blocked is a straight line across. Rounded softens the corners of a block.

subsections.heading: The beard
paragraphs: Leaving it, trimming it, lining it up or taking it off. On my menu, beard work comes with the Signature Cut, so it helps to know before you book.

blocks.heading: What the numbers mean.
rows: Short, a dark shadow of hair
paragraphs: You don't need to memorize these. If you know the number your last barber used, say it. If not, a photo tells me the same thing.

blocks.heading: Bring a picture.
paragraphs: A photo of the cut you want beats any description. Look for one on hair like yours: straight, wavy, curly or coarse hair all wear the same cut differently, so a match on texture tells you more than a match on the celebrity.
Front, side and back views are ideal. If you only have one, a side view shows the fade height and the top length at once.
A photo of what you don't want helps too. If your last cut went too high or too short, show it and say so.

blocks.heading: Point at one.
blocks.lead: Every style page on this site, in a line.

items.title: Low taper fade
items.body: Edges taken down low around the ears and nape, length kept on the sides.

items.title: Skin fade
items.body: Sides blended all the way down to bare skin.

items.title: Burst fade
items.body: A fade that drops to skin in an arc around the ear, keeping length at the back.

items.title: Buzz cut
items.body: One short length all over, or close to it.

items.title: Textured crop
items.body: A short, choppy top pushed forward over short sides.

items.title: Textured fringe
items.body: Longer, piecey hair brought forward over the forehead.

items.title: Curly top fade
items.body: Natural curls on top over faded sides.

items.title: Hard part
items.body: A part line shaved in where your hair naturally divides.

items.title: Slick back
items.body: A longer top combed straight back over shorter sides.

items.title: Modern mullet
items.body: Faded sides with real length kept at the back.

blocks.heading: Book the right service.
paragraphs: If the beard isn't involved, the Essential Haircut ({{price:essential-haircut}}, {{minutes:essential-haircut}}) covers the cut and a straight razor cleanup at the neck. If it is, the Signature Cut ({{price:signature-cut}}, {{minutes:signature-cut}}) has the time built in for a trim or line-up and a hot towel.
Not sure what to call the cut you want? Text the photo to {{phone}} before your appointment and ask.

items.q: How do I ask for a haircut?
items.a: Say how short the sides go, how high the fade starts, how long the top stays, how the neckline is finished, and what happens to the beard. Then show a photo.

items.q: What should I tell my barber if I don't know haircut names?
items.a: Show a picture. A photo of the cut on hair like yours does the explaining for you.

items.q: What's the difference between a fade and a taper?
items.a: A fade takes the sides down short and blends up. A taper only shortens the edges around the ears and at the neckline.
A 2 guard leaves about a quarter inch of hair. Lower numbers leave less, higher numbers more.

tim_questions: Do you work in guard numbers with clients, and are the standard lengths in the table right for your clippers?
